assumptions: THIS INCREMENT adds the CI step 'Print the review tier and lane (informational, gates nothing)' (RFC-2026-034 §8 item 2; RFC-2026-030 §9 item 2 and §10 item 2). It runs the base's copy of scripts/db/classify-review-tier.mjs (with classify-records-only.mjs beside it) before npm ci, prints tier and lane between stop-commands markers and in the escaped, capped job summary, writes no step output and exits 0 on every path; anything other than a full classification prints tier H and lane governance, not classified.

The classifier (WP-0A-DB-00's file, declared amendment) gains laneOf and formatLane: the RFC-2026-034 §2.2 governance path list (each pattern never, guard or additive); a transitive local-import walk read from the head, rooted at every guard, runner, classifier and guard test plus the database runner and harness, with a linear scanner (importSpecs rewritten, which the tier also uses) and fail-closed problems; the fixtures and path literals the harness loads; a test that imports a governance path is governance; audit only with --head-ref on WP-0A-A0-001's branch, equal --repo and --head-repo, and added or modified regular files directly in one evidence/audits/<date>/; records; risk for H and fast for M and L. additive-eligible is printed when only additive-coverable guard paths make the PR governance; it never lowers the lane. Without --lane the output is unchanged on real code.
On this pull request itself the base's classifier has no --lane, so the new step prints not classified (governance); that is the step failing closed, as designed.

security_privacy_cost_impact: Changes CI by one informational step that gates nothing and writes no step output; the classifier gains a print-only lane function. No credential, secret, customer data or provider call; the step runs only the base's copy of the classifier, before any of the pull request's own code.
compatibility_impact: No contract changes: CI, a classifier and tests; no contract-catalog file.
known_limitations: The lane is information for the readers; nothing gates on it yet. The fast lane also needs a module on M_ELIGIBLE_MODULES (RFC-2026-034 §8 item 5) or an L web path, and none exists today.

The import walk is a best-effort aid, not a parser, and does not claim to find every module a guard can load. It fails closed on any symbolic link or gitlink at the head; on an import read from code of a URL other than node:, of an absolute path, or resolving to anything but .js, .mjs, .cjs or .json; and on a reached .ts, .mts, .cts, .tsx, .jsx, .node or .wasm module. Every string in a guard's closure naming a code module joins the walk. Known forms it misses (RFC-2026-007 Amendment 2026-10-11 §D): a path computed at run time; a mechanism naming no repository-relative path literally; a process a guard spawns; a CommonJS require of a file whose extension it treats as data; a literal over the scanner's 4096-character cap; a backslash-separated path; a path held in data the guard reads (for example a JSON file); and a path where node and the walk pick different candidates. Each is an accepted residual: planting it in a guard is a governance edit all four roles read.

Fail closed where the RFC would allow lighter: a module a guard reaches, by import or by a string naming it, is guard kind and not additive-eligible, unless the RFC's additive rule names the path itself (foundation-contract.test.mjs, branch-identity.test.mjs, scripts/test-suite-contract.mjs and scripts/verify-test-coverage-floor.mjs stay additive-eligible). So the database runner's imports lose the mark (the classifier names scripts/db/run.mjs by string), and a file a guard names by string, changed alone, prints governance: scripts/test-suite-contract.mjs names some two dozen test files by literal path (for example catalog-groups.test.mjs and catalog-reference-integrity.test.mjs), and scripts/commit-when-clean.mjs is named too (C0-255r4-1). Test fixture strings make the paths they name governance too (Q0 N-2): none of those paths exists today, but a product file later added at one would print governance. It never lowers a lane; over the last 45 merges no lane changed (R0-255r3-2).
Locally the timeout 300 wrapper is exercised with stand-ins; the real coreutils timeout runs only on CI.
